newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem says Argentina's political risk "nil".
newsitem.headline: Menem says Argentina's political risk "nil".

text.p: Argentina's President Carlos Menem said Monday the decline in the country's risk is thanks to the reduction of political risk to zero.
"Country risk falls when government risk is non-existent. And at this moment government risk is totally nil in Argentina," Menem told a banking conference.

"We have achieved two things that before were a little difficult to install in our community and in the international community: political stability, and thanks to this we have economic stability," he said.
"We have achieved significant stability in our economy which implies an acceptable functioning of the financial system," said the Peronist leader.

Menem pointed out that one consequence was that there are now 140 banks in Argentina, compared with 600 in the 1980s. "The number has fallen but efficiency has increased, which is very important for our country," he said.
Menem added that with the advent of political stability, the previous economic uncertainty that surrounded each and every Argentine election has ended.
"An election is just another election and it is now considered as consolidating something which has cost us so much to achieve: democracy, liberty and human rights," the president said.

"Luckily, country risk has been reduced because government risk does not exist, at the democratic level, but also because we put into action the introduction of the Mercosur in 1991 which has made growth in business possible," he added.
Mercosur is a customs union grouping Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.
